items.difficulty_reason: Block and Markov lower bound for the lamplighter heat kernel with lamps extinguished at their last visits, followed by Fermat-style optimization of the block length. Printed residues kept literal: the exercise asks for p_{2n}(o,o) while the Comment's final display writes p_n(o,o), and since the printed estimate is uniform in n the substitution is a relabelling and not a repair; the block confinement estimate is asserted "for some constant c" rather than derived, which is the book's own standing style for such estimates and leaves no part of the asked target uncovered; and the absorption of ceil(n/r^2) into n/r^2 + 1 together with the assembly of C from c and c_1 is mechanical. Only the bridge from the printed p_n bound to the asked p_{2n}, plus checking that the last-visit lamp-off event is compatible with confinement and return, which the author asserts in one sentence.

statement_spans.source_role: Complete original Exercise6.78, the single counted target: simple random walk on the Cayley graph of the lamplighter group with the standard generators satisfies p_{2n}(o,o) >= exp(-C n^{1/3}) for some C and all n.

proof_spans.source_role: Original Exercise 6.78 with its complete printed author Comment on physical p. 637: the one-block confinement estimate P_v[max_{j<=r^2}|X_j| <= 2r and |X_{r^2}| <= r] >= e^{-c} for every v in [-r,r]; iteration of the Markov property at multiples of r^2 giving P_v[max_{j<=2n}|X_j| <= 2r] >= e^{-c ceil(n/r^2)}; the last-visit lamp-extinguishing on [-2r,2r] together with the return to the origin giving p_n(o,o) >= exp(-cn/r^2 - c_1 r); and the optimisation r = n^{1/3}, closing with the attribution to Pittet and Saloff-Coste (1999). The uncounted context reprints the lamplighter definition (physical p. 106), its exponential growth (physical pp. 106-107), Theorem 6.29 with the sharpness remark (physical pp. 224-225), Corollary 6.32 (physical pp. 225-226) and the book bibliography entry (physical p. 696). No author step is expanded or repaired, no index is synchronised and no hypothesis is altered.

source_roles.literal_source_feature: The group symbol on physical p. 251 is printed as a blackboard-bold capital Z with a script-size circled dot raised above the line, transcribed here as \Z^{\odot}. That reading comes from the root session's own full-resolution viewing of the source page and is not this session's pixel reading; the PDF text layer cannot settle it, because the letter is an unmapped byte of a math-italic font that carries no Unicode map, and the page geometry confirms only that a small circled glyph is raised over a full-size letter. The exercise prints p_{2n}(o,o) and the Comment prints p_n(o,o), both measured as baseline subscripts, and neither index is synchronised. All are transcribed literally and none is repaired or expanded.
